chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn Amr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Aban ibn Taghlib from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) used to command his servants not to slaughter [animals] until the dawn rises, and he would say, 'Indeed, Allah the Exalted has made the night a rest for everything.'
I said, 'May I be your ransom, but if we fear [harm/delay]?' He said, 'If you fear death, then slaughter [immediately].'

key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: may I be your ransom (a phrase of respect)

ai.seo_question: When is the best time to slaughter animals according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sajjad (AS) instructs his servants to delay slaughter until dawn, citing the Quranic principle that night is designated for rest, thereby elevating the act of slaughter to a time of clarity and blessing. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on aligning daily practices with divine wisdom, while offering a pragmatic exception for fear of death or urgent necessity, demonstrating the balance between ritual idealism and practical reality in fiqh.
